title: Migration fact
description: One change of a database's physical shape that its data must follow, with the intent a migration needs to apply it (model/databases/<db>/migrations/open/). A recorded fact has no name, so its file is <lowercase id>.json. Object keys are historical physical keys, not references; a later rekey fact moves them forward. The fact belongs to its database.

name.description: An optional label; a recorded fact has none.

database.description: The database whose shape the fact changes; the fact belongs to it.

after.description: Ids of the facts this one follows, set by the write path: an ordering hint, not a reference. A link to a fact that no longer exists is a warning (MQ4111).

rationale.description: Markdown text: why the element is shaped this way.

decision.description: A URL or a reference (such as ADR-0042) of the decision record. It is not an element id and is not checked.

object.description: The object of a rename, change-type, drop or backfill.

objects.description: The objects of an adopt, baseline, value-map or state-map; context for raw. A value map's objects are the columns that hold the codes.

collections.description: A value map's template-defined collections that hold the codes: each by its owner table's key and attribute, both historical.

from.description: The state before: a rename's name and schema, a change-type's type facets.

via.description: The intermediate names of a folded rename, oldest first.

keys.description: Every key a rekey moved; a column, index, unique, foreign-key or check entry's table is its table's key before the fact.

conversion.description: How a change-type converts stored values: a cast, or an expression per dialect where {table} and {column} expand to quoted names.

cast.description: A plain cast converts the values.

dataCheck.description: The rows the step must not find (a query per dialect; a row stops the step), or why no check is needed.

query.description: The query per dialect; {table} and {column} expand to quoted names.

acknowledge.description: A drop's reason why the data may go.

where.description: A backfill's rows per dialect; without one, the rows where {column} IS NULL.

sql.description: A raw fact's statements per dialect.

skipWhen.description: A raw fact's guard per dialect: a query whose row means the end state already holds.

phase.description: Whether a raw fact runs before or after the schema statements.

referenceType.description: A value-map's reference type, the one that holds the codes after the fact: a historical id, not a reference.

fromReferenceType.description: A value-map of a merge: the reference type merged away, whose codes the fact maps: a historical id, not a reference.

process.description: A state-map's process: a historical id, not a reference.

values.description: Stored codes (or state codes) and their replacements.

held.description: The fact waits: migrators skip it until it is released.

released.description: A held fact may now run.

then.description: Objects, collections and values may be empty (a type rename maps names only); MQ4106 judges the rest.

factKey.description: A historical physical key, as the schema diff matches objects: plain text that is not walked, never a name (it does not start with @ or $).

migrationObject.description: An object by physical key and by its physical names at the time.

table.description: The key of the table a member (a column, index or constraint) belongs to.

schema.description: The database schema name at the time.

tableName.description: A member's table name at the time.

name.description: The object's name at the time.

formerNames.description: The names the object had before: a baseline's objects, and a drop that migration fold joined with the renames before it.

migrationState.description: A side of a fact: names, or a column's type facets and, for a reference column, how its codes are stored. A value map's sides carry its reference type's name and plural name.

pluralName.description: A value map's reference type's plural name, so a pack finds the objects it named after the type.

strategy.description: A reference column's effective storage strategy.

referenceTable.description: The key of the table a reference column's reference type is bound to, at the time.

collection.description: A template-defined collection of a value map: the codes it holds, by its owner table and attribute.

table.description: The owner table's key at the time.

schema.description: The owner table's database schema name at the time.

tableName.description: The owner table's name at the time.

attribute.description: The id of the collection attribute: a historical id, not a reference.

name.description: The attribute's name at the time.

table.description: A column, index, unique, foreign-key or check entry's table key before the fact. An index, unique, foreign-key or check entry moves the constraint's id (a fold into a stereotype); capture keys follow columns.

name.description: The object's name at the time.

value.description: A stored value and its replacement.
